name: sni-rst-stateless
description: A TLS ClientHello naming the relay's cover host draws a single forged RST+ACK toward the CLIENT only — but the box reads just the first data packet of a flow and does not reassemble: a ClientHello whose server_name lies in a second TCP segment passes untouched. Daal's REALITY ClientHello is 600 bytes in one segment, so it is caught.
analogue: Iran's SNI filter as measured by Bock et al. (FOCI 2020), IRBlock (USENIX Sec 2025) and Niere et al. (2025): 'inspects only the first two data-carrying packets of a flow and does not perform full TCP stream reassembly', 'injects RST+ACK toward the client — single-middlebox enforcement'. Model: first data packet only (stricter than the real two), exact name match, one reset toward the client; the server is left with a half-open connection, as there. Not modelled: the certificate SAN/CN second check, case-sensitivity quirks, the fake-SNI/out-of-window tricks that exploit the same statelessness.
